text:
The World Bank's 1997 figures put roughly 60 percent of the world's population in low and lower-middle income countries, which is a bit more than half. This is a recollection, not a checked figure. The $1230 threshold doesn't match the Bank's usual 1997 income cutoffs, so I'm unsure of the exact grouping. If the question counts the Bank's full lower-middle group, the share could be nearer 70 to 75 percent.

CONFIDENCE: 40
